strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout through `cartTotal(items, { coupon })` in src/cart.js: a 10% bulk discount at 10+ items (summing quantities), the SAVE5 coupon applied after the bulk discount with goods floored at $0, refusal of any other coupon, and $4.99 shipping below $50 of discounted goods (free at $50+, nothing for an empty cart). Unit tests in Vitest prove each rule and its boundary through cartTotal. Reading the code, `bulkDiscount` uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount, against AC1; that case is kept as an expected failure and reported as a defect.
inScope: cartTotal pricing: bulk discount, SAVE5 coupon, unknown coupons, shipping threshold, empty cart
Boundaries: 9/10/11 items, goods exactly $50 after discounts, coupon larger than goods
outOfScope: UI or API checkout flows (the repo is a pure pricing library)
assumptions: Totals are compared as numbers rounded to cents, as cartTotal returns them (cents()).
Coupon codes are case-sensitive: 'save5' is 'any other coupon code' and is refused, as the code does.
A non-empty cart whose goods drop to $0 through the coupon still pays $4.99 shipping (goods < $50; only an empty cart costs nothing).
openQuestions: Should a non-empty cart whose coupon brings the goods to $0 still pay $4.99 shipping? The ticket and code both imply yes; the tests assert that.

risks.description: Off-by-one at the bulk threshold: code uses > 10 instead of >= 10, so exactly 10 items gets no discount.
risks.mitigation: TC1 asserts 10 items across lines gets 10% off; kept as expected failure and recorded as a defect.

risks.description: Discount order (coupon before vs after bulk) changes totals.
risks.mitigation: TC4 picks amounts where the two orders give different totals.

risks.description: Shipping threshold checked before discounts or with > instead of >=.
risks.mitigation: TC8 at exactly $50 after a coupon, TC11 where the subtotal is over $50 but the discounted goods are below.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (summing each line's quantity) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets none.
The coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, and the goods never cost less than $0.
Any coupon code other than SAVE5 is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when the goods cost $50 or more after discounts, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs nothing.

defects.title: Bulk discount not applied to a cart of exactly 10 items
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items gets 10% off. bulkDiscount in src/cart.js:22 checks `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so exactly 10 items gets no discount. Should be `>=`.
defects.evidence: cartTotal([{price:10,quantity:6},{price:10,quantity:4}]) returns 100 instead of 90; the test is marked it.fails and passes as an expected failure.

review.standard: Expected values distinguish the rule in the title from plausible wrong implementations
review.summary: The 'exactly $50 after discounts' test uses a $55 subtotal, so an implementation that compares the pre-coupon subtotal with a strict `> 50` also returns 50 and passes. The test only pins the >= boundary for implementations that already use the discounted goods.
review.failureScenario: Implementation: shipping = subtotal(items) > 50 ? 0 : 4.99. For [{price:55,quantity:1}] with SAVE5: 55 > 50 gives free shipping, so the total is 55 - 5 = 50 and the test passes even though both the boundary and the base are wrong. TC11 catches the wrong base, but nothing on its own pins `>=`. Adding a case whose goods are exactly 50 with no discount, e.g. [{price:50,quantity:1}] expecting 50 (54.99 under `>`), would pin the boundary separately.
